claims.text: support-chat-requirements.md: every screen of DonHang.App shows only what it fetched; orderProvider loads an order once and again only when the signed-in customer changes; the app has no timer that asks the API again.
claims.source_hint: docs/team/support-chat-requirements.md @ stage-4 lines 10-14 (opening section, above the excerpt)

claims.text: orderProvider (orders_api.dart 60-65) is a FutureProvider.family (one provider per order id) that watches authProvider and ordersApiProvider and calls fetchOrder(id), watching no timer or server; ordersApiProvider (56-58) builds the OrdersApi object and watches nothing.

Riverpod: a provider that ref.watches another is recomputed when that one changes. A FutureProvider that is not auto-dispose, like orderProvider, keeps its result until then or until invalidated, even with no screen watching; a web page reload restarts the app with fresh state.
claims.source_hint: Riverpod docs: Refs (ref.watch, invalidate); Auto-dispose; Flutter web: page reload restarts the app

claims.text: order_detail_screen.dart watches orderProvider(id) and shows its loading, error or data result.
Requirements: chat needs what the system lacks: the server sends a new message to an already open screen without that screen asking; today customers and shops talk only through Notifications' email.

Scenarios: CT-1 message shows on the other side within 2 s (assumed); CT-2 shop A staff see no other shop's chat; CT-3 dropped connection loses no message, shown on reconnect; CT-4 history kept 12 months (assumed).

CT-5: when the shop replies and the customer is not on the chat screen, the customer gets an email after 5 minutes unread (assumed); email because push needs a phone build ADR 0017 has not made; the file does not reopen ADR 0017.
ADR 0017: stage-4 adds no android/ or ios/ folder to DonHang.App; it is built for the browser only.
The busy-hour rate of about 3.3 orders per second used in the estimate is the team's capacity-plan figure (12,000 orders in one hour).

Estimate: ~3.3 orders/s at peak × 5% (assumed) ≈ 0.17 chats/s; × 600 s (assumed) ≈ 100 open at once, ~200 connections (customer and staff); 10 messages each (assumed) ≈ 1.7 messages/s; the resource to count is connections held open, mostly idle.
Little's law: items in the system at once = arrival rate × average time each stays (used here as open conversations = start rate × open duration).

Ranked drivers: (1) a message reaches an open screen within seconds (CT-1); (2) no message lost when delivery fails (CT-3); (3) staff never see another shop's chats (CT-2); (4) chat never takes capacity ordering needs; the fourth has no CT row and no measure.
Derived: 200 open screens each asking every 2 s make ~100 requests/s, nearly all with nothing new, against ~1.7 messages/s; worth it only when few screens are open or the measure is minutes.

Fetching only when the screen opens fails CT-1 and fits only when messages are read later; a server-sends design sized by open connections fits when a reply must show within seconds; requirements fix the measure, not the mechanism.

Choices: a 30 s measure changes CT-1 first and lets cheaper options pass; push on a closed app is a new requirement until ADR 0017 is revisited; 20% of orders → ~0.66 starts/s, ~400 open, ~800 connections, ~7 messages/s.
Try it: 30-minute conversations → 0.17 × 1,800 ≈ 300 open, ~600 connections, message rate unchanged at ~1.7/s.
DonHang.App's offline queue is sent only on a trigger; queue_sync.dart's comment says 'There is no timer and no backoff'.
